references.text: The Queen of Sheba (the South) came to hear Solomon's wisdom, as told in [ref:1 Kong 10:1-13|1 Kings 10:1-13]. Jesus refers directly to this event when he says that the "Queen of the South" came from the ends of the earth to listen to Solomon.
The parallel account of the Queen of Sheba's visit to Solomon is also found in [ref:2 Krøn 9:1-12|2 Chronicles 9:1-12], which describes her long journey to hear his wisdom.

The parallel passage in [ref:Matt 12:42|Matthew 12:42] contains the same statement from Jesus about the Queen of the South who will stand up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon's wisdom.
[ref:1 Kong 4:34|1 Kings 4:34] tells that people came from all nations to hear Solomon's wisdom, which highlights the wisdom Jesus compares himself to – and says he is greater than.

In [ref:Luk 11:32|Luke 11:32], a similar statement follows about the men of Nineveh who repented at Jonah's preaching, and that something greater than Jonah is here. Together with verse 31, this forms a double testimony that Jesus is greater than these Old Testament figures.

Solomon's proverbs ([ref:Ordsp 1:1-7|Proverbs 1:1-7]) introduce the wisdom for which Solomon was known, and which the Queen of the South came to hear. Jesus claims to be something greater than this wisdom.

Paul writes in [ref:Kol 2:3|Colossians 2:3] that in Christ are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge. This confirms Jesus' words that something greater than Solomon's wisdom is present in him.
[ref:1 Kor 1:24|1 Corinthians 1:24] calls Christ "the power of God and the wisdom of God," which supports Jesus' statement that something greater than Solomon's wisdom is here.

The context in [ref:Luk 11:29-30|Luke 11:29-30] introduces the theme of "this evil generation" seeking a sign, and the sign of Jonah. Verse 31 continues Jesus' judgment on this generation by using the Queen of the South as an example.
